title: Optimized protocol for obtaining and characterizing primary neuron-enriched cultures from embryonic chicken brains
protocol: Analyze eggs by trans-illumination on the 9th day post-fertilization to confirm presence of viable embryo.
Keep analyzed eggs in incubator until next day.
Spray and wipe eggs with 70% ethanol before isolation.
Isolate head from embryonic chicken eggs.
Collect brain tissue from isolated heads.
Place egg in support with air sack facing upward in laminar flow cabinet.
Make a hole through the air sack using scissors.
Increase size of hole using tweezers.
Transfer the embryo from the amniotic fluid to a clean Petri dish on ice using curved tweezers.
Identify the head and dissect the embryo brain using sterile scissors.
Clean the dissected brain with a 1 mL pipette tip and dissection buffer.
Transfer the cleaned brain into a 50 mL tube containing approximately 10 mL of ice-cold dissection buffer.
Grind the collected brain tissue mechanically using a sterile glass Pasteur pipette.
Centrifuge the tissues at 80 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 4-6 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA solution at 37°C, in a water bath.
Homogenize the cell suspension by gently swirling the tube.
Incubate for 5 minutes, then homogenize the cellular suspension by pipetting up and down with a 5 mL serological pipette.
Add 3 volumes of neuron culture medium (at room temperature) to the cell suspension after 10 minutes of incubation.
Filter the cell suspension through a 40 μm nylon cell strainer to remove clumps.
Flush the strainer with 2–3 mL of medium.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 200 × g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 6 mL of ice-cold RBC lysis buffer and incubate for 8 min on ice.
Dilute the cell suspension with 34 mL of PBS.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 270 × g for 10 min, at room temperature.
Repeat with a 4 min-RBC buffer incubation.
Resuspend cells in approximately 16 mL dissection buffer and pass them through a 40 μm nylon cell strainer.
Add 4 mL of Ficoll-PAQUE:PBS (2:1) mixture to a 15 mL tube, at room temperature.
Gently add 4 mL of cell suspension on top of the Ficoll-PAQUE:PBS solution.
Centrifuge at 1,500 × g for 30 min with acceleration and break turned off or set to minimum.
Discard the upper phase and keep the bottom pellet.
Wash the pellet (neuron-enriched cell fraction) with approximately 10 mL of neuron culture medium twice.
Centrifuge at 270 × g for 10 min.
Determine cell number and viability using 0.1% trypan blue.
Seed the cells at 200,000 cells/cm² with appropriate volumes of culture medium per well.
Maintain cultures at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO₂.
Change the culture medium on the 2nd and 5th day after seeding.
Pre-warm the culture medium to 37°C in a water bath.
Remove 50% of the well volume.
Add an equal volume of new culture medium.
Characterization of the neuron-enriched cell fraction by mass spectrometry proteomics.
Adapt the filter-aided sample preparation (FASP) protocol for use.
Prepare samples according to the adapted FASP protocol.
Add 0.9% NaCl solution.
Adjust the volume according to the pellet size.
Use 3 pellet-volumes of NaCl for washing.
Wash cells with 0.9% NaCl solution.
Homogenize tissues in a 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.8 lysis buffer supplemented with 0.05 M DTT, 2% (w/v) SDS, and a protease inhibitor cocktail.
Sonicate the homogenized tissue.
Incubate the sample in a water bath.
Centrifuge the sample to separate supernatant from debris.
Quantify the protein content of the supernatant using a Bradford assay.
Load proteins onto a 3, 10, or 30 kDa Amicon® ultra-centrifugation filter.
Wash retained proteins with an 8 M urea solution in 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Centrifuge to retain proteins on the filter.
Alkalylate the proteins with iodoacetamide.
Wash proteins again.
Digest proteins with trypsin.
Elute peptides from the filter.
Analyze eluted peptides by high-resolution mass spectrometry.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 270 × g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 400 μL of lysis buffer (0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.8, 2% SDS, 0.05 M DTT, and protease inhibitor) to each sample.
Sonicate the samples for 2 minutes.
Incubate the sonicated samples at 95°C for 5 minutes in a water bath.
Cool the samples to room temperature.
Centrifuge the cooled samples at 16000 × g for 10 minutes.
Collect the supernatant.
Quantify the protein content of the supernatant using the Bradford assay with Bio-Rad Protein Assay Dye Reagent.
Load the intended volume of protein solution into a regenerated cellulose membrane Amicon® ultra-centrifugal filter with a 3 kDa molecular weight cutoff (previously washed with water).
Centrifuge the Amicon® at 12 000 × g for 30 minutes at 20°C.
Discard the eluate and wash the retained protein with 200 μL of an 8 M urea solution prepared in 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 30 minutes at 20°C.
Discard the eluate and alkylate the retained protein with 100 μL of 50 mM iodoacetamide in 8 M urea and 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate solution.
Incubate for 20 minutes in the dark.
Centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 30 minutes at 20°C.
Discard the eluate and wash twice the retained proteins with 200 μL of a 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate solution.
Transfer the membrane to a new centrifuge microtube.
Add 100 μL of a trypsin solution prepared in 12.5 mM ammonium bicarbonate buffer to each sample.
Digest the proteins overnight (approximately 16 hours) at 37°C.
Sonicate for 2 minutes, and centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 30 minutes at 20°C.
Add 50 μL of a 3% (v/v) acetonitrile in water containing 0.1% (v/v) formic acid to the membrane.
Centrifuge at 12 000 × g for 30 min at 20°C.
Repeat the addition and centrifugation steps once more.
Collect the eluates from both repetitions.
Analyze the collected eluates by UHPLC-ESI-HRMS.
Alternatively, store the eluates at −80°C until analysis.
Fix the cells with 4% paraformaldehyde dissolved in PBS for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the cells with water three times.
Cover the cells with Mayer’s hematoxylin solution for 8 minutes.
Differentiate the cells with 1% acid ethanol for 30 seconds.
Rinse the cells with saturated lithium carbonate solution for 30 seconds.
Rinse the cells with water.
Dehydrate the cells with 95% ethanol by dipping them for 1 or 2 seconds and allowing all the ethanol to drain and evaporate. Repeat this procedure ten times.
Apply eosin Y for 5 minutes and wash with water.
Cover the cells with toluidine blue solution according to the adapted protocol from García-Cabezas et al. (2016) and Mohd Lazaldin et al. (2020).
Cover the cells with toluidine blue solution for 5 min.
Rinse the cells with water.
Differentiate the cells with 70% ethanol.
Rinse the cells with water.
Cover the cells with Congo red solution for 20 min.
Rinse the cells with water.
Differentiate the cells with alkaline alcohol solution.
Rinse the cells with water.
Observe the stained cells under the microscope.
